title: Zoning-law library, first pass (documents only): every ZR section reachable from the rules the R6B benchmark uses with cross-references followed to the end, the sections the program handles and does not, the sections the remaining options need, and a pitfall checklist from official guidance
objective: Write a documents-only zoning-law library under docs/zoning-law-library/ (extends planned milestone M3; feeds M3-T004/M3-T005, builds no corpus code): (1) benchmark-r6b-sections.json: one entry per ZR section reachable from the sections the R6B-applicable rulesets cite (11-25, 23-22, 23-52, 23-52(b), 23-362, 23-432, 23-344(a)) and from the benchmark's reading (reference cases, NB-06), every cross-reference followed to the end or marked terminal / out of scope with a reason; fields: section_id, title, zr_url, capture_status (snapshot_id + content_digest_sha256 copied from docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/, or NOT CAPTURED), cross_references_out, handled_by (rule-file paths or NOT HANDLED with a reason), coverage_status (the M3-T001 vocabulary), last_amended, notes; (2) cross-reference-closure.md: the traversal; (3) coverage.md: handled and not handled; (4) options-sections.md: for each of the eleven options in the owner-approved order, the ZR sections it needs and whether each is captured and handled; (5) pitfalls.md: a checklist from official guidance (DOB Buildings Bulletins, DOB determinations - project-specific, never generalized - BSA resolutions, the DCP Zoning Handbook), each item with its source, date and link, cited, never bulk-copied; (6) research-log.md: every search, what was found or not, access blocks (nyc.gov PDFs may refuse non-browser fetches: record, never evade), the next step; (7) README.md: what the library is, the unreviewed-draft label (ADR-007), the scope and its limits. Built from the returns of read-only research helpers the orchestrator dispatches (saved outside git) plus the producer's own checks. New captures, registry entries (BSA) and coverage-matrix rows are RECOMMENDED in the report, never made here.
business_reason: The owner (D-094 R102, answer to I1) ordered the zoning-law library started this session beside the report, to stop missing rules: today the program cites seven ZR sections for the benchmark and has no catalog of what it does not handle and no guidance pitfalls.

acceptance_scenarios.given: every ZR section an R6B-applicable ruleset cites
acceptance_scenarios.then: each has an entry whose capture_status matches the snapshot folder (snapshot_id and content_digest_sha256 equal the snapshot's)

acceptance_scenarios.given: every cross-reference named in an in-scope captured section
acceptance_scenarios.then: it is an entry, or marked 'cross-reference not captured' or 'out of scope' with a reason; none is silently dropped
it names exact rule-file paths under services/api/app/rules/rulesets/ or 'NOT HANDLED' with a one-line reason; coverage_status uses the M3-T001 vocabulary

acceptance_scenarios.given: the eleven options in the owner-approved order
acceptance_scenarios.then: each option lists the sections it needs with captured and handled states; none is skipped
it cites an official source (bulletin number and date, a determination with the project-specific caveat, a BSA calendar number, or a Handbook page) with its link; no uncited item; no bulk-copied text

acceptance_scenarios.given: every search the library rests on
acceptance_scenarios.then: each has the source, the query, found / not found / access blocked, the missing item and the next step
only docs/zoning-law-library/** and the producer report changed; no snapshot, registry, coverage matrix or report-lane file
the unreviewed-draft label and direct source links are present; nothing is labelled Verified; no compliant/buildable/feasible claim; unresolved items stay unresolved

risks: nyc.gov asset PDFs refuse non-browser fetches: record BLOCKED with the URL, never evade; cite by reference.
Following cross-references can fan out across the whole ZR: bound the first pass to the R6B + C2-2 benchmark frontier and the eleven options, and record out-of-scope terminals explicitly.
Public repository: pointers and short quotes with provenance only, no bulk third-party text.
path_notes: Lane L (library), disjoint from the report lane; docs/zoning-law-library/ is covered by Lane C's docs/** ownership rule (no OWNERSHIP.yaml change). Research helper returns are saved in the session folder outside git and cited in research-log.md.
